notes.fentanyl:
Concentration reference

Stock: 50 mcg/mL. Workbook preparation options: 12.5, 25 or 50 mcg/mL; default 25. Patient-specific mixing is also available. These are workbook choices, not established universal veterinary standards or maximums.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.
notes.lidocaine:
Concentration reference

Stock: 2% = 20 mg/mL. Workbook preparation options: 10 or 20 mg/mL. Use an appropriate plain injectable formulation without epinephrine; verify suitability for IV infusion. These options are not universal veterinary maximums. Feline CRIs remain disabled.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.
notes.ketamine:
Concentration reference

Assumed stock: 100 mg/mL. Workbook preparation options: 1, 5 or 10 mg/mL; default 10. These are workbook choices, not universal veterinary maximums. Product formulations differ; the linked human Ketalar label requires dilution of its 100 mg/mL product before IV administration.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.
notes.insulin:
Concentration reference

Stock: U-100 regular insulin = 100 U/mL. Final concentration is calculated from patient weight, prescribed dose and pump rate. For comparison, the human Humulin R label specifies 0.1–1 U/mL in 0.9% NaCl for IV use. This is product-label guidance, not a validated veterinary DKA maximum; veterinary protocols may use other dilutions. Review preparations outside the product-label range and follow your line-priming protocol.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.
notes.reglan:
Concentration reference

Stock: 5 mg/mL. Final concentration varies with weight, daily dose, syringe duration or bag pump rate. No single fixed concentration is assumed for all patients. The product label confirms stock strength; it does not establish a universal veterinary CRI maximum.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.
notes.norepinephrine:
Norepinephrine concentration

Assumed stock: 1 mg/mL = 1,000 mcg/mL norepinephrine base. Verify the actual vial. Diluent: D5W per workbook; confirm product compatibility and stability.

Workbook comparison options: 8, 16, 32 and 64 mcg/mL. Peripheral 16 / central 64 mcg/mL are retained workbook guardrails, not validated veterinary maximums. No universal veterinary maximum was substantiated in the reviewed veterinary sources.

A veterinary case series reports peripheral vasopressor extravasation injury and supports central access when feasible and consideration of lower concentrations. Concentration alone does not establish line safety.
